what_it_does: This paper presents a specialized processor for smartphone image upscaling (making a small photo larger and clearer). The challenge has three parts: (1) the neural network inference (the computation) produces overlapping regions that require huge amounts of on-chip storage, (2) simple low-bit-width number formats crush image quality, and (3) upsampling operations (which expand an image) are computationally wasteful if you reuse the same hardware as downsampling. The solution uses a novel compact number format (pseudo-FP6) that captures high precision despite using just 6 bits per number, fuses multiple neural-network layers to minimize buffer memory, and uses a streamlined upsampling datapath that avoids redundant math.
